title: Future Continuous
tagline: in progress at a future time: will be + -ing
why: Use it to say what you will be in the middle of at a time in the future, and to ask polite questions about people's plans. It sounds natural and friendly in everyday English.
know: the form will be + verb-ing: I'll be working
time phrases like at 8 pm tomorrow, this time next week and when you arrive
understand: the difference between an action in progress at a future time and a single future action
why Will you be using the car? sounds softer and more polite than Will you use the car?
able: say what you will be doing at a certain time tomorrow or next week
ask politely about someone's plans before you ask a favour
mistakes: This time tomorrow I will working.
This time tomorrow I will be working.
Will you using the car tonight?
Will you be using the car tonight?
At 9 pm I will be watch the game.
At 9 pm I will be watching the game.
Next week I will to be travelling.
Soon I will be knowing the answer.
use: An action in progress at a time in the future: At 10 am tomorrow, I'll be sitting in a meeting.
An action that will be in progress when something else happens: When you land, I'll be waiting at the gate.
Polite questions about plans: Will you be using the printer this afternoon?
Things that will happen anyway, as part of a plan or routine: I'll be passing the bank, so I can drop it off.
form: I will be working. / She'll be travelling.
We won't be staying long. / He will not be coming.
Will you be using the car? / What will you be doing at 6?
Yes, I will. / No, I won't.
signals: at 8 pm tomorrow, this time next week, at noon on Friday, when you arrive, all day tomorrow, in two hours, still
tip: Think of a photo taken in the future: When you arrive, I'll be eating (I'm in the middle of it). Compare When you arrive, I'll eat (I start then). State verbs like know, want and own don't take -ing.

pick.q: Please don't phone me at 8 pm tomorrow. I ___ my son's hockey game.
pick.why: 8 pm tomorrow is a future time and the game will be in progress: will be + -ing. The answer is will be watching.

pick.q: This time next week, we ___ on a beach in Cuba.
pick.why: This time next week is in the future, so use will be + -ing: will be lying. Don't forget be.

pick.q: ___ you be using the meeting room after lunch? I need it for a call.
pick.why: A polite question about plans: Will + subject + be + -ing. The answer is Will.

pick.q: When your plane lands, I ___ for you at the arrivals exit.
pick.why: The waiting will already be in progress when the plane lands: will be waiting. After be, use the -ing form.

pick.q: I can't join the 3 o'clock call. I ___ a client in Mississauga then.
pick.why: At 3 o'clock the visit will be in progress: will be visiting. After will, use be, not been.

pick.q: Don't worry about the noise tonight. We ___ the drill after 6 pm.
pick.why: The negative is won't (will not) + be + -ing: won't be using.

pick.q: At midnight on December 31, thousands of people ___ in Nathan Phillips Square.
pick.why: At midnight the party will be in progress: will be celebrating. After be, add -ing.

pick.q: Don't ask me now. I ___ the answer tomorrow morning.
pick.why: Know is a state verb, so we don't use it with -ing. The answer is will know.

type.q: This time tomorrow, I ___ (fly) to Calgary.
type.why: This time tomorrow + an action in progress: will be flying (or I'll be flying).

type.q: When you get home at midnight, the children ___ (sleep).
type.why: They will already be asleep when you arrive, so the action is in progress: will be sleeping.

type.q: Don't call at 7. We ___ (have) dinner then.
type.why: At 7 dinner will be in progress: will be having (or we'll be having).

type.q: Don't worry, I ___ (not / sleep) when you call at 11 pm. I always stay up late.
type.why: Negative future continuous: won't be sleeping (or will not be sleeping).

type.q: What do you think you ___ (do) at this time next year?
type.why: At this time next year asks about an action in progress then: will be doing (or you'll be doing).

type.q: When the guests arrive at 7, I ___ (still / cook).
type.why: Still goes after will: will still be cooking. The cooking will be in progress when the guests arrive.

type.q: At this time next Saturday, my sister ___ (walk) down the aisle.
type.why: At this time next Saturday + action in progress: will be walking.

type.q: At 3 pm tomorrow, I ___ (sit) in a job interview, so I can't pick up the kids.
type.why: At 3 pm tomorrow the interview will be in progress: will be sitting (or I'll be sitting).

spot.q: This time tomorrow I will be fly over the Atlantic.
spot.why: After will be, use the -ing form: will be flying.

spot.q: Will you using the car on Saturday morning?
spot.why: The question needs be: Will you be using the car?

spot.q: At 9 pm tonight, we will watching the hockey final.
spot.why: Don't forget be: will be watching.

spot.q: Next Monday at 10, she is be presenting her report to the board.
spot.why: Future continuous uses will, not is: will be presenting.

spot.q: This time next year, I will be knowing much more English.
spot.why: Know is a state verb, so no -ing: will know.

order.a: Will you be using the car tonight?
order.why: Question: Will + you + be + -ing: Will you be using the car tonight?

order.a: I will be working from home tomorrow.
alt: Tomorrow I will be working from home.
order.why: Subject + will be + -ing: I will be working from home tomorrow.

order.a: What will you be doing at this time next week?
order.why: Wh- question: What + will + you + be doing + time phrase.

order.a: They will be waiting for us at the airport.
alt: They will be waiting at the airport for us.
order.why: Subject + will be waiting + for us + place.

pick.q: At 6 am tomorrow, I ___ to work on the 401.
pick.why: At 6 am tomorrow the drive will be in progress: will be driving.

pick.q: ___ you be going to the grocery store later? We're out of milk.
pick.why: A polite question about plans: Will you be going...? The answer is Will.

pick.q: Sorry, I can't help you move on Sunday. I ___ a double shift at the hospital.
pick.why: On Sunday the shift will be in progress: will be working.

pick.q: Don't come at 2. The cleaners ___ the floors then.
pick.why: At 2 the washing will be in progress: will be washing. Don't forget be.

pick.q: We ___ any visitors next week because my wife is having surgery.
pick.why: Next week is future: won't be having. The negative is won't + be + -ing.

pick.q: I'm sure you ___ the new apartment once you move in.
pick.why: Love is a state verb, so we don't use -ing: will love.

type.q: At 7:30 tomorrow morning, I ___ (stand) at the bus stop in the snow.
type.why: At 7:30 tomorrow the action will be in progress: will be standing (or I'll be standing).

type.q: When you wake up tomorrow, your father ___ (drive) to Ottawa.
type.why: He will already be on the road when you wake up: will be driving.

type.q: I ___ (not / use) my laptop this evening, so you can borrow it.
type.why: Talking about plans: won't be using (or will not be using). Won't use is also possible.

type.q: Don't wait for me at 6. I ___ (still / work) on the budget.
type.why: Still goes after will: will still be working.

type.q: This time on Friday, we ___ (camp) in Algonquin Park.
type.why: This time on Friday + action in progress: will be camping (or we'll be camping).

type.q: The kids ___ (play) outside when you get here, so ring the bell loudly.
type.why: The playing will be in progress when you arrive: will be playing.

type.q: At noon tomorrow, Ahmed ___ (write) his final exam.
type.why: At noon tomorrow the exam will be in progress: will be writing.

type.q: From 9 to 5 on Monday, the technicians ___ (repair) the elevator, so please use the stairs.
type.why: The work will be in progress all day Monday: will be repairing.

spot.q: At 4 pm I will be meet my new boss.
spot.why: After will be, use -ing: will be meeting.

spot.q: Are you be staying with your cousins in Halifax?
spot.why: The question starts with Will: Will you be staying?

spot.q: Tomorrow at this time, I will to be sitting on a train.
spot.why: No to after will: will be sitting.

spot.q: Soon we will be owning our own house.
spot.why: Own is a state verb, so no -ing: will own.

order.a: We will be staying with friends in Montreal.
alt: We will be staying in Montreal with friends.
order.why: Subject + will be staying + with friends + place.

order.a: Will you be going to the party on Friday?
order.why: Question: Will + you + be going + place + time.

order.a: She will be studying all weekend for her exam.
alt: She will be studying for her exam all weekend.
order.why: Subject + will be studying + time + purpose.

bank.q: Don't visit at 10 am tomorrow. I ___ yoga at the community centre.
bank.why: At 10 am tomorrow the class will be in progress: will be doing.

bank.q: ___ you be using your ladder this weekend? I want to clean my gutters.
bank.why: A polite question about plans: Will you be using...?

bank.q: Tomorrow at 5 pm, my husband ___ the kids up from school.
bank.why: At 5 pm tomorrow the action will be in progress: will be picking.

bank.q: Next Monday at this time, I ___ my first shift at the new job.
bank.why: Next Monday at this time the shift will be in progress: will be working.

bank.q: Sorry, I ___ my phone during the funeral tomorrow. I'll call you back after.
bank.why: Negative future continuous: won't be checking. Don't forget be.

bank.q: When the movie starts at 9, we ___ popcorn in the lobby.
bank.why: The buying will be in progress when the movie starts: will still be buying.

bank.q: Next year Jun ___ a car of his own.
bank.why: Have meaning own is a state verb, so no -ing: will have.

bank.q: At 11 tonight, most of the city ___ .
bank.why: At 11 tonight the sleeping will be in progress: will be sleeping.

bank.q: This time tomorrow, we ___ (drive) through the Rockies.
bank.why: This time tomorrow + in progress: will be driving (or we'll be driving).

bank.q: At noon tomorrow I ___ (not / sit) at my desk. I'll be at lunch.
bank.why: Negative future continuous: won't be sitting (or will not be sitting).

bank.q: At 10 tomorrow night, I ___ (still / pack) for my trip.
bank.why: Still goes after will: will still be packing.

bank.q: At this time next month, my parents ___ (enjoy) the sun in Florida.
bank.why: At this time next month + in progress: will be enjoying.

bank.q: When you come out of the doctor's office, I ___ (sit) in the car outside.
bank.why: The sitting will already be in progress when you come out: will be sitting.

bank.q: Will you be coming to the barbecue on Sunday?
bank.why: This sentence is correct. Will you be coming...? is a polite question about plans.

bank.q: At 7 tomorrow evening, I will be cook for twelve people.
bank.why: After will be, use -ing: will be cooking.

bank.q: When you call at noon, I will be teaching a class.
bank.why: This sentence is correct. The class will be in progress when you call: will be teaching.

bank.q: Don't call at 9. We will watching the news then.
bank.why: Don't forget be: will be watching.

bank.a: Will you be working late tonight?
bank.why: Question: Will + you + be working + late + tonight.

bank.a: I will be thinking of you on your big day.
alt: On your big day I will be thinking of you.
bank.why: Subject + will be thinking + of you + time.

bank.a: Our flight will be landing at noon tomorrow.
alt: Our flight will be landing tomorrow at noon.
bank.why: Subject + will be landing + time.
